rationale: A consistently links actions to inputs and also initiates sensible shifts: touch→lean-in (t8), call→orient (t20), food offer→approach and wait (t32–41), buzzer→lean away and monitor (t68–77), and object presentation→sustained focus on ball (t44–53), with spontaneous yet coherent reorientations (e.g., to mirror t18, chime t30, cube t54, person t94). B shows some initiative (play-bow to person t14–17; to ball t37–42) and a plausible fatigue arc (lies down t43 onward), but often fails to adapt to salient inputs: call (t20) increases arousal without reorienting, food offer (t32) is ignored, and startle (t68) elicits virtually no change while prone. Overall, A appears more autonomous, coherent, and adaptively responsive across the timeline.
